subject: SLA rebase & burst-latency grace period - pilot negotiation
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@horizon-analytics.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T15:22:00Z
Subject: Request: SLA rebase for burst inference workloads

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the quick demo last week — the dedicated routing and prefix cache look promising. As we scope the pilot I wanted to surface one operational constraint on our side and ask whether Redwood can make a temporary exception in the SLA template for bursty inference workloads.

Our infra profile: nightly batch runs and unpredictable customer-driven spikes during market opens. The baseline p95 latency target for interactive requests is fine at your default SLA, but the aggregated burst traffic causes our p99 to oscillate and pushes utilization beyond the plan you initially quoted. Practically speaking we would like:

- A limited SLA rebase for the first 90 days of the pilot: standard uptime remains 99.95%, but the monthly availability band that triggers monetary remedy would be softened from 99.95 -> 99.9 for the pilot period only.
- A temporary increase in the monthly credit cap to cover the expected variability, with credits paid monthly based on observed hours below the pilot band.
- Two operational requirements: (1) a shared latency/tail dashboard (read-only) and (2) a guaranteed export of request traces for spike windows (for post-mortem).

I attached our SLO forecast for the next 3 months (Horizon-SLO-forecast.xlsx) to show expected traffic patterns.

Can Redwood accept a 90-day pilot with these carve-outs? If so we can loop legal and push for an expedited amendment.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Platform
Horizon Analytics

Attachment: Horizon-SLO-forecast.xlsx
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@horizon-analytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: SLA rebase for burst inference workloads

Marta — thanks for the context and the forecast. Quick read-through looks helpful. A few clarifying items so we can scope an internal proposal: 

1) Pilot traffic: can you confirm expected peak qps and % of total traffic contributed by the spikes (ballpark is fine)? that helps sizing reserved capacity and estimating the remedy exposure.
2) Credits model: do you want a dollar-equivalent monthly cap (e.g., $Xk / month) or a percentage-of-invoice cap? most customers prefer percentage but we can accommodate either.
3) Tracing: we can provide a daily export for windows you nominate; is a 72-hour retention for exported traces sufficient for your post-mortem?

Internally cc'ing Laura (sales lead) for commercial terms and Aditya (runtime/product) for operational feasibility on tracing and dashboard access. I also forwarded the SLO spreadsheet to the infra team.

If agreeable, Laura and I will propose a narrow SLA amendment for a 90-day pilot with: (a) a rebased availability trigger of 99.9% for pilot months only, (b) monthly crediting with a defined cap, (c) explicit monitoring/tracing exports and (d) an automatic revert to standard SLA at pilot end unless both parties agree to extend.

I’ll draft the initial commercial language once we lock the cap approach.

—Karthik
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@horizon-analytics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T09:30:00Z
Subject: Proposed 90-day SLA pilot amendment (Horizon Analytics)

Hi Marta — appreciate the detail and the SLO file. We ran a quick headcount/expense check on our side and propose the following narrow amendment structure to support a 90-day pilot: 

Summary (pilot terms):
- Pilot duration: 90 days from the signed amendment start date.
- Availability trigger (pilot months only): remedies apply only if monthly availability < 99.9%. Outside pilot months standard SLA (99.95%) applies.
- Monthly credit model: credits computed as % of monthly invoice (not to exceed 20% of the month’s invoice). Credits paid monthly in the invoice following the observed month.
- Latency: we will not change baseline latency SLOs, but for pilot months we will exclude scheduled nightly batch windows (specifiable in calendar) from p99 trigger calculations to avoid false positives during planned heavy jobs.
- Monitoring & exports: read-only dashboard link (view-only) + daily trace export for any window you flag within 72 hours. We’ll provide a simple export manifest and S3 path.
- Revert & extension: pilot reverts to standard SLA after 90 days unless both parties sign an extension amendment.

Operational guardrails:
- We require a joint runbook for spike windows (owner, on-call contact, escalation path).
- If spikes exceed the projected qps by >40% for two consecutive weeks, Redwood reserves the right to recommend provisioning changes (additional dedicated capacity).

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether you prefer a dollar cap or % cap — we recommend the % cap above to keep reconciliation simple.
2) If accepted, we’ll circulate a short amendment (PDF) for signature. I’ve attached the draft amendment for review (draft-SLA-amendment.pdf) and opened a DocuSign envelope to speed sign-off: https://docusign.net/HZN-SLA-Amendment-2026

If the high-level terms look OK, we’ll loop legal for a minimal redline and aim to have this signed and operational within 5 business days of agreement.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
laura@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: draft-SLA-amendment.pdf
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@horizon-analytics.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Proposed 90-day SLA pilot amendment (Horizon Analytics)

Laura — this looks reasonable and thank you for structuring the pilot clearly. Two quick asks before we sign: 

1) Fallback model variant & capacity: can the amendment explicitly call out a fallback path (i.e., during sustained spikes Redwood will fallback to a smaller model variant with documented degradation characteristics) so our product team can map UX expectations?
2) Tracing SLA: we need the exported traces to include request_id, model_variant, timestamp, and latency buckets; can you confirm the CSV/Parquet manifest will include those columns?

We prefer the percentage-based cap (20%) you proposed. Subject to the two clarifications above we are happy to sign the amendment — please add the fallback/model-variant clause and confirm the trace manifest columns and I’ll ask Legal to sign DocuSign.

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Platform
Horizon Analytics
